title: Anuak Fish and Sorghum
community: Anuak people — Gambella region, the Nile tributaries
author: Chef Haile

heritage.origin: Anuak people — Gambella region along the Baro River (Nile tributary)
heritage.history: The Anuak are a Nilotic people living in the Gambella region of western Ethiopia, where the Baro River (a major Nile tributary) provides abundant fish. Their cuisine centres on river fish, sorghum, and wild foods from the lowland forest — completely different from the highland Ethiopian traditions. The Anuak have traditionally been primarily fishermen and farmers, and their fish preparations use minimal spice, relying on the freshness of the catch and simple cooking techniques. They have cultural connections to the Nuer, Dinka, and other Nilotic peoples of South Sudan.

desc: Anuak River Fish with Sorghum — fresh Baro River fish simply grilled or stewed with garlic, tomato, and chilli, served with sorghum porridge. The cuisine of the Nilotic Anuak people — minimal spice, maximum freshness, completely unlike highland Ethiopian food.
longDesc: Anuak fish with sorghum represents one of Ethiopia's most distinct food traditions — the Nilotic river culture of the Gambella lowlands where Nile-connected rivers provide the freshest fish and sorghum provides the starch.
ingredients: 600g fresh river fish — whole or fillets
steps: Make sorghum porridge: bring water to boil. Whisk in sorghum flour. Cook stirring 15 minutes until thick.
Grill or pan-fry fish with garlic, tomato, chilli, and oil.
chefTips: Anuak food is the most minimally spiced in Ethiopia — freshness is the flavour.
cookingScience: See ETH081 for fish cooking science.
sustainabilityTips: Baro River fish — sustainably caught from a major Nile tributary.
healthBenefits: Very lean protein from river fish.
culturalNote: Anuak fish and sorghum is the food of the western Ethiopia Nile corridor — the connection between highland Ethiopia and the great Nile Valley, expressed in the simplest possible preparation.
